newsitem.title: PAKISTAN: Pakistan court rejects Bhutto sacking challenge.
newsitem.headline: Pakistan court rejects Bhutto sacking challenge.

text.p: Pakistan's Supreme Court refused on Tuesday to accept ousted prime minister Benazir Bhutto's petition against her sacking, saying it contained "frivolous...and scandalous matter".

Bhutto's lawyer, Aitzaz Ahsan, said he was surprised by the court action on the petition, which he filed last Wednesday to challenge the dissolution of the National Assembly (lower house) and Bhutto's dismissal by President Farooq Leghari on November 5 on disputed charges of corruption and misrule.
The court said the petition had been returned for modifications or the petitioner could challenge Tuesday's refusal within 14 days.
However, the court will begin a preliminary hearing on Wednesday of another petition filed by National Assembly Speaker Yousaf Raza Gilani, which also challenges Leghari's action.
A court official had earlier declined to specify the objectionable portions of Bhutto's petition.

But a long court statement issued later listed several pages of the 42-page petition that it said contained objectionable portions, including blistering criticism of Leghari for dismissing his former political patron.
The court rebuff came just as police arrested Bhutto's political secretary Naheed Khan on unspecified charges in the latest of a series of arrests since her sacking.
The court statement said references to the president and the chief justice should be made in proper language.

"As this petition has been drafted in an argumentative manner...and contains frivolous, unnecessary and scandalous matter, it is not entertainable and is hereby returned...for making necessary modifications," it said.
Earlier, Ahsan said in the Punjab province capital Lahore that the Supreme Court's specific objections had not been brought to his notice, and added: "I am no doubt surprised."
Asked if he would remove the objectionable portions and file the petition again, Ahsan said he would go to the court in Islamabad on Wednesday to see what to do next.
Ahsan said the petition had been drafted with "due deference and utmost respect and humility" bearing in mind the petitions and judgements in two similar dismissals that were not upheld by courts.

Bhutto's was the fourth government to be overturned by a president in less than nine years by the use of controversial powers inserted in Pakistan's constitution by the late military ruler General Mohammad Zia-ul-Haq.

The Supreme Court had upheld none of the previous dismissals and reinstated a government led by former prime minister Nawaz Sharif in 1993 a few weeks after then president Ghulam Ishaq Khan had dismissed it.

Naheed was arrested by officers from the Federal Investigation Agency police at Islamabad airport as she arrived with Bhutto from the southern city of Karachi, a spokesman for Bhutto said. It was not clear where she was headed.
There was no police comment on the arrest.

Bhutto's spokesman, Shah Mahmoud Qureshi, said Naheed had been detained under a Maintenance of Public Order Ordinance, the same law authorities have used to detain Bhutto's husband Asif Ali Zardari since November 5, but he did not know how long she would be held.
Other people already arrested include Nawaz Khokhar, the former science and technology minister, intelligence bureau chief Masood Sharif and several other government officials.
